subject: Slow-path accounting during CDN peering maintenance - request for exception/reconciliation
messages:
From: David Choi <david.choi@novatech.com>
To: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 17 Sep 2026 08:42:00 -0700
Subject: Severe slow-path latency impacting NovaTech - request for SLA reconciliation

Hi Lauren,

We saw a sustained increase in completion latency starting ~2026-09-17T07:30Z across our production cluster that routes through Redwood's CDN peering path. Avg completion latency doubled and a subset (~12% of requests) timed out at 10s during that window. Our telemetry correlates the impact to the same region where you run the peering with OrbitCDN.

I've attached a CSV of our client-side probes (filename: probe-logs-20260917.csv). Can you confirm what maintenance or configuration changes were scheduled on Redwood's side or with any peering partner for that period? We're evaluating an SLA credit and need a timeline and rationale.

Thanks — this is high impact for our billing window.

David Choi
Head of Platform, NovaTech
David.Choi@novatech.com

Attachments: probe-logs-20260917.csv (CSV, 1.2MB)

From: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Severe slow-path latency impacting NovaTech - request for SLA reconciliation

Hi David — thanks for the heads up and for sending the probe logs. I'm escalating to SRE (Marissa) and our partner ops contact at Orbit (Samantha) to get an immediate timeline.

Quick ask: Marissa, can you correlate NovaTech's probe timestamps with our edge and backbone telemetry and share an initial cause analysis?

Samantha — could you confirm whether Orbit had any scheduled peering maintenance or BGP flaps in the us-west peering region around 2026-09-17 07:00-09:00Z? If you have a maintenance manifest please attach.

I'll follow up with a proposed remediation/credit approach once we have the technical readout. Appreciate the quick turnaround — Lauren

From: Samantha Lee <samantha.lee@orbitcdn.com>
To: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>, David Choi <david.choi@novatech.com>
Cc: "Peering Ops" <peering-ops@orbitcdn.com>
Date: Fri, 18 Sep 2026 02:12:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Severe slow-path latency impacting NovaTech - request for SLA reconciliation

Hi all,

Orbit confirmed a short, targeted peering maintenance for route redistribution in us-west at 2026-09-17T07:15Z to 2026-09-17T07:45Z UTC. Maintenance was announced on our portal and we attached the maintenance manifest for traceability (orbit-maint-manifest-0917.json).

We do see some retransmits and transient latency spikes on our side during the window; however, our edge logs indicate the majority of traffic returned to baseline before 07:50Z. That said, if your probe data shows continued elevated tail latency past 08:00Z we will work with Redwood to map handoffs.

Orbit's position is that targeted peering maintenance is a third-party event; we will cooperate on evidence.

Regards,
Samantha Lee
Senior Network Engineer, OrbitCDN
Attachments: orbit-maint-manifest-0917.json (JSON, 45KB)

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>, David Choi <david.choi@novatech.com>, Samantha Lee <samantha.lee@orbitcdn.com>
Date: Fri, 18 Sep 2026 09:34:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Severe slow-path latency impacting NovaTech - request for SLA reconciliation

Lauren / Karthik — initial tech note from SRE after correlating logs:

- Summary: NovaTech's client probes show a tail-latency spike beginning ~2026-09-17T07:28Z UTC and persistent elevated p95/p99 until ~2026-09-17T08:12Z UTC.
- Redwood edge telemetry: our egress to Orbit peering saw route churn beginning ~07:15Z (matches Orbit manifest) and a second spike of retransmits & queueing on the slow-path beginning ~07:44Z and tapering off by 08:05Z.
- Important detail: NovaTech's traffic for that customer is sticky to a small subset of edge nodes due to geographic hashing; because of that, transient peering issues amplified into sustained client-observed degradation.
- Attribution: portion of the initial spike (07:15–07:45Z) aligns cleanly with Orbit's maintenance window. The extended slow-path behavior (07:45–08:05Z) correlates to internal route reconvergence and elevated queue backpressure on our slow-path lanes.

Recommendation for remediation and crediting:
- We consider the initial 07:15–07:45Z to be third-party peering maintenance (Orbit). Per SLA, third-party documented maintenance is an exception for uptime credits only if the vendor's maintenance was properly announced and manifested. Orbit has provided a manifest.
- For the residual window 07:45–08:05Z, Redwood's runtime experienced slow-path queueing that contributed materially to tail-latency and timeouts. We recommend an apportionment approach: 60% of the measured impact attributable to Redwood's slow-path behavior, 40% attributable to Orbit. Operationally that would map to a 60% SLA credit (of the impacted-window pro-rated credit) from Redwood.

Action items:
1) Karthik — please prepare the credit calculation and a short customer note offering the apportionment-based credit and a remediation summary.
2) Stephanie — please confirm language for an exception (we will note third-party maintenance + Redwood remediation).
3) Lauren — propose we offer NovaTech the 60% credit now with a joint Orbit/Redwood RCA to close. If NovaTech disputes, escalate to account exec for negotiation.

Quoted below is a sample metric extract from our egress telemetry for the edge node that handled ~72% of NovaTech's p99 traffic: 
> 2026-09-17T07:35Z p99: 2.3s (baseline 0.8s)
> 2026-09-17T07:50Z p99: 1.9s (baseline 0.8s)
> 2026-09-17T08:02Z p99: 0.95s (baseline 0.8s)

Marissa Cole
SRE Lead, Redwood Inference
--
Attachments: (none)

From: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
To: David Choi <david.choi@novatech.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Samantha Lee <samantha.lee@orbitcdn.com>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 20 Sep 2026 16:12:00 -07:00
Subject: Proposed resolution: apportionment credit + joint RCA for Sep 17 outage

Hi David — thank you for your patience while we investigated. Short summary and proposed resolution: 

- Root cause: A targeted OrbitCDN peering maintenance (07:15–07:45Z) initiated route churn; Redwood experienced secondary slow-path queueing after route reconvergence that extended client-observed tail latency until ~08:05Z.
- Proposed customer remediation: Redwood will apply a pro-rated SLA credit for the impacted window. Following SRE analysis, we propose Redwood covers 60% of the impacted window credit value and Orbit accepts responsibility for 40% (we will request Orbit's published reimbursement to NovaTech). Practically, Redwood will issue NovaTech a 60%-of-window credit now to expedite remediation.
- Next steps: 1) If this is acceptable, please reply with an approval so Karthik can schedule the credit to your account. 2) We will produce a joint RCA (Redwood + Orbit) and share a postmortem link within 5 business days. 3) We will add an operational mitigation (adjusted route hashing for NovaTech's prefix) to reduce exposure to single-edge amplification.

If you disagree with the apportionment, we can escalate the credit discussion to your account exec and our commercial team, but we'd like to resolve quickly to reduce billing impact.

Thanks — Lauren
Senior Manager, Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference

Attachments: link to probe logs and internal telemetry (see related_links)
